newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore gas oil rises on buying interest.
newsitem.headline: Singapore gas oil rises on buying interest.

text.p: Singapore gas oil prices rose despite lower crude prices and bearish American Petroleum Institute (API) distillate stocks as buyers pushed up prices and on keen buying interest from China, traders said.

They said Chinese buyers were rushing to use up their import quotas this year and were actively buying gas oil swaps with December traded at $32.03, up 20 cents from Tuesday. Traders said China recently bought end-December lifting physical gas oil at $250 a tonne, c+f south China. Physical gas oil was again bid up by two traders--a Swiss trader at $32.60 for Dec 20-24 and a local trader at $32.30 Dec 21-25, 20 cents over Tuesday bids.
A European major again offered at $32.45 for Dec 30-Jan 3 lifting fob.
Jet fuel market was boosted by expectations of higher regional demand ahead of the Chinese and Moslem festive seasons in February.
A 10,000-tonne jet fuel parcel was traded between two European majors at 33-cents per barrel over Singapore quotes for end-December lifting fob.
Both light distillates were steady with lack of clear direction. Naphtha was stymied on talks of the Singapore Refining Co's January allocation only due on Thursday.

Gasoline buyers and sellers were also quiet but the market was expected to remain under pressure in December as traders kept prices low whilst pricing in cargoes for Taiwan. Traders said the naphtha/gasoline spread, currently quoted as low as $1.50 per barrel, may even narrow further, prompting refiners to sell their gasoline at a higher price, at a premium of $3.25 a barrel over naphtha spot quotes, instead of gasoline related.

Fuel oil was steady on balanced demand and supply fundamentals in a thin year-end market. A cargo of 180 centistoke fuel oil for Dec 26-30 lifting was offered at $124 a tonne. -- Singapore Newsroom (+65-870 3084)
